name: success_shaped_failure
predicate: Does a reachable failure path produce a return value, metric, event, or state that represents successful authoritative work?
required_context: Target, failure contract, and relevant callers/callees or metric semantics.
positive: A failed authoritative query becomes an empty successful result; successful-egress telemetry fires before a failed send.
negative: A documented optional cache miss falls back to the authoritative source; metrics explicitly count attempted work.

name: invalid_state_accommodation
predicate: Does internal code accommodate representations excluded by an established input contract?
required_context: Normalization boundary, target, and internal input contract.
positive: After normalization into a struct, private helpers independently accept nil, atom-key maps, and string-key maps.
negative: A public compatibility adapter intentionally accepts several representations.

name: test_claim_gap
predicate: Can an obvious incorrect implementation of the behavior covered by this test or supplied suite pass all its assertions?
required_context: Test/suite, implementation under test, fixtures and assertion helpers.
positive: Cookie object-key tests use only keys requiring no encoding; removing key encoding survives. A missing-key branch has no distinguishing assertion.
negative: A narrowly described smoke test; assertions delegated to helpers; a test uses discriminating boundary inputs.

name: semantic_duplicate
predicate: Does the target independently reimplement a supplied existing domain operation without a meaningful contract difference?
required_context: Both implementations and their consumers or contracts.
positive: A test repeats the same server/user/backend setup already supplied by a canonical helper.
negative: Similar operations enforce different policies or deliberately coexist during migration.

name: process_without_runtime_reason
predicate: Does a process merely organize code without needed state ownership, coordination, isolation, concurrency limits, or lifecycle?
required_context: Whole process module, supervision/ownership and callers.
positive: A GenServer serializes independent pure calculations solely for namespacing.
negative: A coordinator owns resources and timers even if it also exposes a simple getter.

name: policy_free_abstraction
predicate: Does the target add indirection or configurability without a distinct contract, supported variation, or useful boundary?
required_context: Layer, consumers, configuration and intended policy.
positive: An internal option and several helpers only route to the same required export policy.
negative: A stable public facade, external adapter, or useful test seam with one implementation.

name: derived_state_drift
predicate: Are two representations of the same fact independently maintained with a visible path that can make them disagree?
required_context: Initialization and all relevant update paths.
positive: A removal callback updates the collection but leaves its stored count unchanged.
negative: A consistently updated body-length accumulator avoids repeatedly traversing accumulated data; a deliberate historical snapshot has different semantics.

name: disguised_state_machine
predicate: Do independently stored booleans encode mutually constrained states of one domain concept with reachable meaningless combinations?
positive: Loading, loaded and failed flags can simultaneously remain true for one operation.
negative: Independent feature capabilities or flags with separate meanings.

name: timing_instead_of_synchronization
predicate: Does elapsed time stand in for observing completion or establishing required ordering?
required_context: Sleep/timer, asynchronous operation, and test/lifecycle contract.
positive: Sleep before checking a worker write and assume it has finished.
negative: A delayed server deliberately triggers a receive-timeout test; actual debounce or expiry behavior is under test.

name: presentation_only_authorization
predicate: Is a restriction confined to rendering/navigation while the corresponding server action lacks equivalent authorization?
required_context: UI restriction, action/event handler, and authorization in called context functions.
positive: Hide a delete button but accept arbitrary delete events without a server-side check.
negative: The action calls an authorization-enforcing context or scoped lookup.

name: framework_reimplementation
predicate: Does custom code duplicate an available project framework facility without materially different semantics?
required_context: Custom code, installed dependency version, and supplied facility documentation.
positive: A parallel casting and validation pipeline duplicates the supplied Ecto changeset contract.
negative: The required semantics differ or the installed dependency lacks the feature.

name: semantic_comment_noise
predicate: Does an implementation comment only paraphrase obvious adjacent code, adding no rationale, invariant, warning, or constraint?
positive: A comment repeats that fetch_users fetches users.
negative: A comment explains why ordering matters, why a simpler implementation fails, or documents a public API.

name: avoidable_repeated_traversal
predicate: Does a loop repeatedly traverse growing accumulated data to recover information maintainable locally without changing behavior?
required_context: Loop initialization, recursive transitions, length limits, and underlying traversal semantics.
positive: Compute the length of the entire accumulated iodata at every received chunk.
negative: Maintain a consistently updated length counter or compute a genuinely new value.

name: redundant_wrapper
predicate: Can the marked wrapper be replaced by its input without changing any output, exception, or other observable behavior?
required_context: Complete wrapper, patterns and exhaustive alternatives.
positive: An exhaustive case returns every matched value unchanged including its catch-all.
negative: A non-exhaustive identity case raises on unmatched input; map reconstruction drops extra keys; a result tuple is unwrapped.

name: client_state_round_trip
predicate: Does a LiveView interaction wait for a server round trip solely to change transient presentation state that can be changed locally without altering application behavior?
required_context: Complete template, event handler, JS commands or hooks, consumers of the affected assigns, and any data loading, authorization, persistence, shared state, or URL/navigation contract.
positive: Opening an already-rendered help modal pushes an event whose only effect is toggling a visibility assign; no server operation needs that state.
negative: Opening a modal fetches authorized data, starts real work, persists shared state, or changes meaningful URL state. JS.show/hide runs locally even when composed with an independent JS.push.

name: liveview_reconnect_state_loss
predicate: Does a concrete disconnect/reconnect or LiveView remount lose user input or workflow state that the feature must retain, because its recovery path cannot reconstruct that state?
required_context: Mount and parameter callbacks, state transitions, rendered form fields and IDs, phx-change and recovery bindings, client hooks, storage or URL state, installed LiveView behavior, and the retention contract.
positive: A wizard removes earlier fields from the DOM and stores their values only in assigns; remount resets those values and recovery submits only the current step, losing required earlier input.
negative: A stable form ID and phx-change restore all needed inputs through built-in recovery; custom recovery, persisted drafts, or URL state reconstruct the workflow. Disposable UI state intentionally resets. A missing custom reconnect hook alone is not a defect.

name: per_record_database_read
predicate: Does loading one collection perform avoidable database reads per record, so query count grows with collection size when a batch or suitable join could preserve the required semantics?
required_context: Collection query, loops and called helpers/components, association schemas and loaded state, filters, tenant/authorization scopes, pagination or per-parent limits, and query behavior or measurements.
positive: After fetching posts, Enum.map calls a helper that preloads each unloaded author separately, adding one database query per post.
negative: Repo.preload on the whole list batches an association; query preloads use a fixed number of queries; already-loaded associations cause no new read. Separate batched queries can outperform a join, especially for has-many data. Distinct required per-record semantics cannot be dropped just to reduce query count.
